title: How Costco Actually Makes Money
notes: say = what the narrator speaks. show = caption text. '|' splits caption chunks (same count in say and show). {name} marks a cue at the start of the next spoken word. *text* in show is highlighted.

lines.say: In nineteen eighty-five, {hotdog}a hot dog and a soda | at Costco cost {price}one dollar fifty.
lines.show: In 1985, a hot dog and a soda | at Costco cost *$1.50.*

lines.say: {inflation}Adjusted for inflation, | it should cost {four}more than four dollars.
lines.show: Adjusted for inflation, | it should cost *more than $4.*

lines.say: But Costco has {refused}refused to raise that price | for {forty}over forty years. | And that tells you everything | about {title}how this company really makes money.
lines.show: But Costco has refused to raise that price | for *over 40 years.* | And that tells you everything | about how this company *really* makes money.

lines.say: Last year, {sold}Costco sold almost | {num}three hundred billion dollars' worth of stuff.
lines.show: Last year, Costco sold almost | *$300 billion* worth of stuff.

lines.say: {strange}But here's the strange part. | It kept only about {cents}three cents | of every dollar as profit.
lines.show: But here's the strange part. | It kept only about *3 cents* | of every dollar as profit.

lines.say: {cap}Costco famously caps its markup | at around {fourteen}fourteen percent, | {fifteen}fifteen for its own Kirkland brand.
lines.show: Costco famously caps its markup | at around *14 percent,* | *15* for its own Kirkland brand.

lines.say: {low}So prices stay low, | and {back}shoppers keep coming back.
lines.show: So prices stay low, | and shoppers keep *coming back.*

lines.say: {where}So where does the money | actually come from?
lines.show: So where does the money | *actually* come from?

lines.say: To shop at Costco, | {need}you need a membership. | It starts at {fee}sixty-five dollars a year | in the U.S., | and {members}more than eighty-four million members | pay for one.
lines.show: To shop at Costco, | you need a *membership.* | It starts at *$65 a year* | in the U.S., | and more than *84 million members* | pay for one.

lines.say: {adds}That adds up to {fees}nearly six billion dollars | a year in fees. | {nocost}And unlike groceries, | those fees cost Costco very little to collect.
lines.show: That adds up to *nearly $6 billion* | a year in fees. | And unlike groceries, | those fees cost Costco *very little* to collect.

lines.say: {side}Put it side by side: | those fees are worth {twothirds}nearly two-thirds | of Costco's entire annual profit.
lines.show: Put it side by side: | those fees are worth *nearly two-thirds* | of Costco's entire annual profit.

lines.say: {renew}And around {nine}nine in ten members renew, | every single year.
lines.show: And around *9 in 10* members renew, | every single year.

lines.say: {groc}The cheap groceries. | {fuel}The cheap fuel. | {dog}The one-fifty hot dog.
lines.show: The cheap groceries. | The cheap fuel. | The *$1.50* hot dog.
